subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 9-month-old girl is brought in for poor feeding and an enlarging abdomen. Her length is at the 10th percentile, and she has a protuberant abdomen with a liver edge 7 cm below the costal margin. After a 4-hour fast, glucose is 36 mg/dL, lactate 7.1 mmol/L, uric acid 9.6 mg/dL, and triglycerides 460 mg/dL; liver biopsy shows increased amounts of glycogen with normal structure. Serum cortisol and growth hormone are normal.
question: Deficiency of which of the following enzymes is most likely responsible for this presentation?
explanation_correct: Glucose-6-phosphatase in the endoplasmic reticulum of hepatocytes (and renal tubular cells) catalyzes the final step of both glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, releasing free glucose into the blood. Its deficiency (von Gierke disease, glycogen storage disease type I) causes severe fasting hypoglycemia, lactate accumulation as glucose-6-phosphate is shunted into glycolysis, hyperuricemia, and hypertriglyceridemia with massive hepatomegaly.

explanation_incorrect.A: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase 1 deficiency also causes fasting hypoglycemia and lactic acidosis, but glucose release from glycogenolysis remains possible and hyperuricemia with massive glycogen accumulation is not typical.
explanation_incorrect.B: Pyruvate carboxylase deficiency impairs gluconeogenesis from lactate and alanine but produces lactic acidosis with failure to thrive and neurologic symptoms, and glycogen stores are not increased.
explanation_incorrect.C: Phosphoenolpyruvate carboxykinase deficiency impairs gluconeogenesis but not glycogenolysis, and the pattern of massive glycogen accumulation with hyperuricemia is not seen.
explanation_incorrect.D: Liver glycogen phosphorylase deficiency (Hers disease) causes hepatomegaly and fasting hypoglycemia, but it is not associated with prominent lactic acidosis and hyperuricemia.

educationalObjective: Glucose-6-phosphatase deficiency (von Gierke disease) causes fasting hypoglycemia, lactic acidosis, hyperuricemia, and hypertriglyceridemia with hepatomegaly because the liver cannot release glucose from either glycogenolysis or gluconeogenesis.
